  kṛtpratyayās triprakārāḥ #1 kṛtyā niṣṭhāghañādayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
---
SP (Verse redaction)
<s>Kṛt</s> suffixes (verbal derivatives) are of three kinds: <s>kṛtya</s> (potential participles), <s>niṣṭhā</s> (past participles), and those beginning with <s>ghañ</s>.

children.text:
(SPS:) "kṛtyāḥ" kṛtyapratyayāḥ #2 "niṣṭhādayaś" ca #3 "ghañādayaś" ca,
dvandvāt paro #4 hi śabdaḥ pratyekam abhisambadhyate //
children.translated_text:
(SPS commentary:) '<s>Kṛtyāḥ</s>' means <s>kṛtya</s>-suffixes; 'and those beginning with <s>niṣṭhā</s>'; 'and those beginning with <s>ghañ</s>' —
for the word following a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) connects individually with each [member].

children.text:
***NOTES:
#1 N: tiŚ; #2 N: ŚpratyaŚ s.m. in margina.; #3 N: Śś ca s.m. in margina.; #4 N: puŚ;
children.translated_text:
***NOTES:
#1 N: tiŚ; #2 N: ŚpratyaŚ added in the margin; #3 N: Śś ca added in the margin; #4 N: puŚ;
SD (Prose redaction)
SP (Verse redaction)
The <s>kṛtya</s> [suffixes] are mostly just five: <s>tavya</s>, <s>anīya</s>, <s>ya</s> (from <s>kyap</s>), <s>ghya</s> (from <s>ghyaṇ</s>).

children.text:
(SPS:) yady api tavaikekenyatvā #6 ity ete 'pi kṛtyās, tathāpi #7 lakṣye prayo-
gādarśanān naivaite #8 kṛtyā ity etadartham uktaṃ #9 "prāyaḥ pañcaive"ti //
children.translated_text: (SPS commentary:) Although <s>tavaikekenyatvā</s> [Pāṇini 3.4.14] — these too are <s>kṛtya</s> [suffixes], nevertheless, since they are not observed in usage in literary works, they are indeed not [counted as] <s>kṛtya</s> — for this purpose it is said 'mostly just five.'

children.text:
SD
(11r:) [bhā]ve utpadyante. bhāvasya dhātvarthamātrasya sāmānyarūpatvād eka-
tvāc ca bhāve prathamaikavacanam eva bhavati, yathā 'tena, tābhyām, taiḥ, tva-
yā, yuvābhyām, yuṣmābhiḥ, mayā, āvābhyām, asmābhiḥ vā, bhavitavyam'.
evaṃ liṅge kartari, napuṃsakaliṅge ca, sākalyād bhedāḥ.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
They arise in the sense of <s>bhāva</s> (impersonal action). Since <s>bhāva</s>, being merely the meaning of the verbal root, has a general nature and is singular, only the nominative singular occurs in <s>bhāva</s> [usage], as in 'By him, by those two, by them, by you, by you two, by you all, by me, by us two, or by us — it must be done (<s>bhavitavyam</s>).' Similarly in the case of gender — in agent [usage], in neuter gender — due to comprehensiveness, [there are] variations.
SP (Verse redaction)

children.text: ete cākarmakād dhātor utpadyante yadā, tadā /
children.translated_text: When these [suffixes] arise from an intransitive (<s>akarmaka</s>) root, then,
due to the unity of the verbal meaning, the first [case], singular number, applies to them;

children.text: 'bhavitavyaṃ tvayā, tena, tābhyāṃ, tair vā, tayā' yathā //
children.translated_text: as in '<s>bhavitavyaṃ tvayā, tena, tābhyāṃ, tair vā, tayā</s>' (it must be done — by you, by him, by those two, by them, or by her).

children.text:
SD
27 sakarmakāt tu kṛtyapratyayāḥ karmaṇi bhavanti. tadā karmaṇaḥ kriyāyāś ca
parasparasambandhe sati, karmābhihitaṃ bhavati / abhihite karmaṇi liṅgārtha-
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
But from a transitive (<s>sakarmaka</s>) root, <s>kṛtya</s> suffixes apply in the sense of the object (<s>karman</s>). Then, when there is mutual connection between the object and the action, the object is denoted. When the object is denoted, [depending on] the meaning of gender alone,

children.text: mātre, prathamā bhavati / tadā ca karmānusāreṇa triliṅgatvam 27, [yathā] #10 27
children.translated_text: the first case (nominative) applies. And then, in accordance with the object, [the form takes on] three genders, as in

children.text: 'tena grāmo gantavyaḥ, tena nagaraṃ gantavyam 27, tena nagarī gantavyā' 27 //
children.translated_text: '<s>tena grāmo gantavya���</s>' (the village must be gone to by him), '<s>tena nagaraṃ gantavyam</s>' (the city must be gone to by him), '<s>tena nagarī gantavyā</s>' (the town must be gone to by him).
SP (Verse redaction)

children.text: sakarmakād amī dhātor utpadyante yadā, tadā /
children.translated_text: When these [suffixes] arise from a transitive root, then,
their gender, number, and case [agreement is] in accordance with the object.
'<s>gantavyo bhavatā grāmo</s>' (the village must be gone to by you), '<s>gantavyā nagarī tvayā</s>' (the town must be gone to by you),
'<s>gantavyaṃ nagara��� tena</s>' (the city must be gone to by him) — [thus is] the construction of examples.

***NOTES:
#10 Ms: <s>te(11v)na</s>;

children.text:
SD
kṛtyapratyayānāṃ kartari kadācit ṣaṣṭhī bhavati, kadācit tṛtīyā bhavati, yathā
'tasya, tena vā, bhavitavyam / tasya, tena vā, grāmo gantavyaḥ'.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
With <s>kṛtya</s> suffixes, sometimes the sixth case (genitive) applies to the agent, sometimes the third case (instrumental), as in '<s>tasya, tena vā, bhavitavyam</s>' (by him / of him, it must be done); '<s>tasya, tena vā, grāmo gantavyaḥ</s>' (by him / of him, the village must be gone to).

children.text:
SD
tavyānīyau [~Pāṇ 3.1.96], svarād yaḥ [~Pāṇ 3.1.97], vṛ-dṛ-juṣi-iṇ-śasu-stu-
guhāṃ #11 kyap [~Pāṇ 3.1.109], ṛvarṇavyañjanāntād ghyaṇ [~Pāṇ 3.1.124],
bhāvakarmaṇoḥ kṛtyakhalarthā [~Pāṇ 3.4.70] ity ete pratyayāḥ bāhulyena
vartamāne kāle pañcamyarthe, [']numatau vidhau vā, bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
<s>Tavya</s> and <s>anīya</s> [Pāṇini 3.1.96], <s>ya</s> after vowels [Pāṇini 3.1.97], <s>kyap</s> after <s>vṛ</s>, <s>dṛ</s>, <s>juṣ</s>, <s>iṇ</s>, <s>śas</s>, <s>stu</s>, and <s>guh</s> [Pāṇini 3.1.109], <s>ghyaṇ</s> after [roots ending in] <s>ṛ</s>-vowels or consonants [Pāṇini 3.1.124], and '<s>bhāvakarmaṇoḥ kṛtyakhalarthā</s>' (in the sense of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>karman</s>, <s>kṛtya</s> and <s>khal</s> [suffixes]) [Pāṇini 3.4.70] — these suffixes generally [apply] in the present tense, in the sense of the fifth [case], in the sense of permission, or in the sense of injunction.

***NOTES:
#11 Ms: ŚjuṣīṇŚ;

children.text:
SD
anumatiḥ praśnapūrvako [']ṅgīkāraḥ, yathā 'kim ahaṃ grāmaṃ gacchāmi, na
vā'. sa(12r:)mpraty ucyate #12, 'tvaṃ grāmaṃ gaccha, tvayā grāmo gantavya' iti
vā.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
Permission (<s>anumati</s>) is acceptance preceded by a question, as in 'Shall I go to the village or not?' Thereupon it is said: 'You go to the village,' or '<s>tvayā grāmo gantavyaḥ</s>' (the village must be gone to by you).

***NOTES:
#12 Ms: <s>ūcŚ</s>;

children.text:
SD
vidhir ajñātajñāpanaṃ, yathā 'tvaṃ grāmaṃ gaccha, tvayā grāmo gantavya' ity
uktāḥ kṛtyapratyayāḥ.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
Injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is the making known of what is unknown, as in '<s>tvaṃ grāmaṃ gaccha</s>' (you go to the village), '<s>tvayā grāmo gantavyaḥ</s>' (the village must be gone to by you) — thus the <s>kṛtya</s> suffixes have been stated.
SD (Prose redaction)
The <s>niṣṭhā</s> [suffixes] and the rest are now stated. '<s>Kta</s> and <s>ktavatu</s> are designated <s>niṣṭhā</s>' [Pāṇini 1.1.26]; <s>kvansu</s> [Pāṇini

3.2.107], <s>kāna</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.106], <s>śatṛṅ</s>, <s>ānaś</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.124], <s>ki</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.171], <s>u</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.168], <s>ukañ</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.154], <s>iṣṇu</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.136], <s>ktvā</s> [Pāṇini 3.4.18], <s>khal</s> [Pāṇini 3.3.126], <s>yuś</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.148], <s>ānaṅ</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.128], <s>tṛṇ</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.135], <s>vuṇ</s> [Pāṇini 3.2.146], <s>ṇin</s> [Pāṇini 3.1.134] — and so forth: these are the <s>niṣṭhā</s> and the rest.

SP (Verse redaction)
The <s>niṣṭhā</s> and the rest are remembered as <s>kta</s>, <s>ktavatu</s>, <s>kvansu</s>, <s>kāna</s>, and the rest.
(SPS commentary:) 'And the rest' [includes] those beginning with <s>śatṛṅṅ</s>.

***NOTES:
#13 N: ŚktarvanŚ; #14 N: ŚnsuŚ added in the margin; #15 Ś: āŚ destroyed; #16 N: ŚṅṅaŚ in the margin;

children.text:
SD
tatra ktapratyayas sarvadhātūnām akarmakāṇām atīte kāle bhāve utpadyate. tatra
napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ prathamaikavacanam eva bhavati, yathā 'tenāsitam' 27.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
Therein, the <s>kta</s> suffix of all intransitive roots arises in the sense of <s>bhāva</s> (impersonal) in the past tense. There, only the neuter nominative singular occurs, as in '<s>tenāsitam</s>' (by him it was sat = he sat).

SP (Verse redaction)
In the past sense, for intransitive [roots], the <s>kta</s> suffix is prescribed in the <s>bhāva</s> sense.
Due to the unity of the verbal meaning, its [form is] nominative singular, as in:

children.text: 'āsitaṃ tena, tābhir vā, tābhyāṃ, tair vā, tvayā, mayā' //
children.translated_text: '<s>āsitaṃ tena, tābhir vā, tābhyāṃ, tair vā, tvayā, mayā</s>' (it was sat — by him, by them [f.], by those two, by them [m.], by you, by me).
(SPS commentary:) '<s>Prathamaikavacaḥ</s>' means the nominative case, singular number.

***NOTES:
#17 Ś: ŚveŚ ktaŚ destroyed; #18 Ś: After <s>prathaŚ</s>, three <s>akṣaras</s> destroyed; #19 N: omits from <s>dhātvŚ</s> to <s>yathā</s>;

children.text:
SD
sakarmakāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ (12v:) ktapratyayo [']tīte kāle karmaṇy eva bhavati, na
tu bhāve. tatra karmābhihitaṃ bhavati / karmānusāreṇa ktapratyayāntasya triliṅ-
gatvam, yathā 'tenaudanaḥ #20 bhuktaḥ 27, tena 27 śikhariṇī bhuktā, tena
bhuṭitraṃ #21 bhuktam' iti.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
The <s>kta</s> suffix of transitive roots arises in the past tense in the sense of the object (<s>karman</s>) only, not in the sense of <s>bhāva</s>. There, the object is denoted. In accordance with the object, the <s>kta</s>-suffixed form takes three genders, as in '<s>tenaudanaḥ bhuktaḥ</s>' (rice was eaten by him), '<s>tena śikhariṇī bhuktā</s>' (the <s>śikhariṇī</s> [a curd dish] was eaten by him), '<s>tena bhuṭitraṃ bhuktam</s>' (the <s>bhuṭitra</s> [a baked bread] was eaten by him).
SP (Verse redaction)

children.text: yadā sakarmakāṇāṃ ktaḥ #22 karmaṇy utpadyate, tadā /
children.translated_text: When <s>kta</s> of transitive [roots] arises in the sense of the object, then,
its gender, number, and case [agree] in accordance with the object.

children.text: 'bhuktā drākṣā, phalaṃ bhuktaṃ, bhuktas tenaudano' yathā #23 //
children.translated_text: '<s>bhuktā drākṣā</s>' (the grape was eaten), '<s>phalaṃ bhuktam</s>' (the fruit was eaten), '<s>bhuktas tenaudano</s>' (rice was eaten by him) — as [examples].

children.text:
***NOTES:
#20 Ms: tenodaŚ; #21 Ist hier "bhaṭitraṃ" (pw: 'am Spiesse gebacken',
Bhāvaprakāśa 2.20) zu lesen? - A/W: 'The word is obviously a Sanskritization. It
could be that it refers to "bhaṭurā/baṭurā" (from "bhaṭṭhā/bhaṭṭhi" 'kiln, oven'
which, in turn, may be from "bhrasj"), a type of "nān"/bread commonly used in the
Punjab-Jammu area, and that MW, etc. have not understood the nature of the
eatable exactly. The same dictionaries explain "śikhariṇī" as a dish made of curds,
sugar, and spices, but the obvious cognate "śikaraṇ" current in Marathi stands
primarily for crushed bananas or plantain fruits mixed with milk and sugar'.; #22 Ś:
statt ktaḥ: aŚ ; #23 Ś: om. bhuktā bis yathā.;
children.translated_text:
***NOTES:
#20 Ms: <s>tenodaŚ</s>; #21 Is '<s>bhaṭitraṃ</s>' (as per pw: 'roasted on a spit,' Bhāvaprakāśa 2.20) to be read here? — A/W: 'The word is obviously a Sanskritization. It could be that it refers to "bhaṭurā/baṭurā" (from "bhaṭṭhā/bhaṭṭhi" meaning kiln, oven, which in turn may be from "bhrasj"), a type of "nān"/bread commonly used in the Punjab-Jammu area, and that MW, etc. have not understood the nature of the eatable exactly. The same dictionaries explain "śikhariṇī" as a dish made of curds, sugar, and spices, but the obvious cognate "śikaraṇ" current in Marathi stands primarily for crushed bananas or plantain fruits mixed with milk and sugar'; #22 Ś: instead of <s>ktaḥ</s>: aŚ; #23 Ś: omits from <s>bhuktā</s> to <s>yathā</s>;
SD (Prose redaction)

children.text: niyatānām eva dhātūnāṃ ktapratyayaḥ kartari bhavati // gatyarthākarmaka #24-
children.translated_text: The <s>kta</s> suffix applies in the agent sense only for a restricted set of roots: '<s>gatyarthākarmaka</s>-
<s>śliṣa-śīṅ-sthāsa-vasa-ruha-jana-jīryatibhyaś</s>' [Pāṇini 3.4.72] — and so forth.

children.text:
SP
  'maitro grāmaṃ gata' iti prathamokte 'tra kartari /
children.translated_text:
SP (Verse redaction)
'<s>Maitro grāmaṃ gataḥ</s>' (Maitra has gone to the village) — here, [the <s>kta</s> suffix is] prescribed in the agent sense.

***NOTES:
#24 Ms: ŚākarmāŚ;

children.text:
SD
ktavantupratyayo [']karmakebhyas sakarmakebhyo vā dhātubhyo [']tīte kāle kar-
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
The <s>ktavantu</s> suffix, from either intransitive or transitive roots, in the past tense, always

children.text: tary eva bhavati / na kadācid bhāvakarmaṇoḥ ktavantupratya(---[Bl.13 fehlt]).
children.translated_text: arises in the agent sense only — never in the senses of <s>bhāva</s> or <s>karman</s> does the <s>ktavantu</s> suffix [arise] (lacuna — folio 13 missing).
[continuation:] ...meaning' — thus the <s>niṣṭhā</s> and the rest have been stated in summary.

children.text:
SP
  kartary #25 eva ktavantuḥ #26 syān, na kvacid bhāvakarmaṇoḥ //
children.translated_text:
SP (Verse redaction)
The <s>ktavantu</s> [suffix] applies only in the agent sense, never in [the senses of] <s>bhāva</s> or <s>karman</s>.
Its gender, number, and case [agree] in accordance with the agent.
'<s>Bhuktavān odanaṃ caitraḥ</s>' (<s>Caitra</s> has eaten rice [m. sg.]), '<s>nārī bhuktavatī</s>' (the woman has eaten [f. sg.]), '<s>kulam</s>
<s>bhuktavat</s>' (the family has eaten [n. sg.]), '<s>puruṣā bhuktavantaḥ</s>' (the men have eaten [m. pl.]) — thus is the determination.

***NOTES:
#25 N: <s>kartayeva</s>; #26 N: ŚvaktuŚ; #27 Ś: Four <s>akṣaras</s> after ŚsaṅkhyāŚ partially destroyed; #28 Ś: The following 21 <s>akṣaras</s> almost completely destroyed;
SD (Prose redaction)
The <s>ghañ</s> [suffixes] and the rest are now stated. <s>Vuṇ</s>, <s>tṛc</s> [Pāṇini 2.1.133], <s>ghañ</s> [Pāṇini
3.3.16], <s>yuṭ</s> [Pāṇini 3.3.115], <s>kti</s> [Pāṇini 3.3.95] — such and the like are the <s>ghañ</s> and the rest.

children.text:
SP
  ghañādisaṅgrahas tv eṣa #29 uktvāitān vakṣyate 'dhunā /
children.translated_text:
SP (Verse redaction)
Having stated these [<s>niṣṭhā</s> suffixes], the collection of <s>ghañ</s> and the rest will now be stated.
(SPS commentary:) 'These' means the <s>niṣṭhā</s> and the rest.

***NOTES:
#29 N: <s>eṣā</s>; #30 Ś: <s>Śādīnām</s>;

children.text:
SD
vuṇtṛcāv akarmakebhyas sakarmakebhyo vā dhātubhyo vartamāne kāle kartary
evotpadyete, na bhāvakarmaṇoḥ.
children.translated_text:
SD (Prose redaction)
The suffixes <s>vuṇ</s> and <s>tṛc</s>, from either intransitive or transitive roots, arise in the present tense in the agent sense only — not in [the senses of] <s>bhāva</s> or <s>karman</s>.

children.text:
SP
  yau vuṇtṛcau pratyayau, tau kartary eva, na cānyayoḥ //
children.translated_text:
[Verse (SP):]
The two suffixes <s>vuṇ</s> and <s>tṛc</s> are [used] only in the sense of the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), and not in [the sense of] the other two.
(Commentary [SPS]:) 'The other two' [means] <s>bhāva</s> (action itself) and <s>karman</s> (object).

children.text:
anayor akarmakatvam #31 utpannayoḥ kartary evābhihite prathamā / yathā bhava-
tīti 'bhāvako #32 devadattaḥ, devadatto bhavitā' /
children.translated_text: When these two [suffixes], being intransitive, are derived in the sense of the agent only, the nominative [case] is used. For example: '<s>bhavati</s>' [gives] '<s>bhāvaka</s> is <s>Devadatta</s>,' [and] '<s>Devadatta</s> is <s>bhavitā</s> (one who will be).'

[Verse (SP):]
In '<s>bhāvako Maitra</s>' and such [examples], the nominative [denotes] the unexpressed object.
(Commentary [SPS]:) The same should be understood for <s>tṛc</s> [suffix].

***NOTES:
#31 Ms: <s>anayoḥ karma</s>-. Text according to interlinear correction.; #32 Ms: <s>bhāvuko</s>; #33 Ś: <s>bhāvuko</s>; #34 Ś: -<s>kartari</s>;

children.text:
SD
anayor vuṇtṛcos sakarmakatvam utpannayoḥ kartari prathamā, karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī,
yathā 'devadattaḥ odana(14v:)sya pācakaḥ, devadattaḥ odanasya paktā' iti. vuṇ-
tṛcoḥ ca kartranusāreṇa triliṅgatvam, yathā 'sa odanasya pācakaḥ, sā pācikā, tat
kulam odanasya pācakam' iti / 'sa paktā, sā paktrī, tat kulam odanasya paktṛ'.
children.translated_text:
[Prose (SD):]
When these two [suffixes] <s>vuṇ</s> and <s>tṛc</s>, being transitive, are derived in the sense of the agent, the nominative [is used for the agent], and the genitive for the object. For example: '<s>Devadatta</s> is the cooker (<s>pācaka</s>) of rice,' '<s>Devadatta</s> is the cooker (<s>paktā</s>) of rice.' yatra tu kriyāpadaṃ kiṃcit svarūpeṇa nopāttaṃ #79, tatrāstir bhavantīparo [']dhy-
āhriyata #80 iti bhāṣyakāravacanaprāmāṇyāt #81 asti, bhavati, vidyate iti vā sattā-
sāmānyavāci kriyāpadam adhyāhṛtya, vākyārthapratiṣṭhāne[na] #82 bhāvyam.
sattā hi sarvabhāvānām antaraṅgā, yathā 'vṛkṣa' iti kevalapade ukte, asti,
bhavati, vidyate iti vā gamyate. (17v:) atra vā astīti kriyāsāmānyavāci
dhātūpalakṣaṇaparam.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
But where some verbal form is not employed in its own form, there, on the authority of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>'s statement that "<s>asti</s> (is), <s>bhavati</s> (becomes), [or <s>vidyate</s> (exists)] is supplied," a verbal form denoting general existence (<s>sattāsāmānyavācin</s>) such as <s>asti</s>, <s>bhavati</s>, or <s>vidyate</s> [is understood].
SP (verse)

children.text: astikriyā prayoktavyā yatra na śrūyate kriyā /
children.translated_text: The verb <s>asti</s> (to be) should be supplied where no verb is heard; /

children.text: 'prāpnoti sa naro mokṣaṃ, yasya bhaktir harau' #83 yathā //
children.translated_text: as in '<s>prāpnoti sa naro mokṣaṃ, yasya bhaktir harau</s>' (that man attains liberation who has devotion to <s>Hari</s>). //

SD
kvacic ca prakaraṇānusāreṇa viśiṣṭāpi kriyādhyāhriyate, kartṛrahitāyāḥ
kriyāyā abhāvāt.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
And sometimes, in accordance with the context, even a specific verb is supplied, because an action without an agent does not exist.

children.text:
SD
evaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ vākyaṃ kvacin muktaka ekaṃ bhavati, kvacid dve vākye, kvacid
bahūni vākyāni / prabandhe tu bahūny eva vākyāni bhavanti. teṣāṃ ca vākyā-
nāṃ parasparasambaddhatopādeyā, na ced unmattavākyatvaprasaṅgāt, yathā
'kuṇḍam a(18r:)jājinaṃ palalaṃ sphaiyakṛtasya #84 putra' iti #85.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
Thus, a sentence of this nature is sometimes a single independent sentence (<s>muktaka</s>), sometimes two sentences, sometimes many sentences. In continuous discourse (<s>prabandha</s>), however, there are indeed many sentences. And their mutual connection (<s>parasparasambaddhatā</s>) is to be adopted; if not,
SP (verse)

children.text: evaṃbhūtaṃ kvacid vākyam ekaṃ, dve vā, bahūni vā /
children.translated_text: A sentence of this nature is sometimes one, or two, or many, /

children.text: vaktum arthaṃ samarthāni, sambandhaś cet parasparam /
children.translated_text: [and they are] capable of expressing [their] meaning, if there is mutual connection; /
otherwise, [the result would be] the madness [of utterances like] '<s>kuṇḍaṃ palālam</s>' (a pot, straw). //

***NOTES:
#84 Ms: <s>spheyaŚ</s>; #85 Cf. <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> 1.1.1 (p.38);

children.text:
SD
parasparasambandhaś ca svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena #86 vā bhavati,
sarvanāmaparāmṛṣṭārthamukhena vā.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
And the mutual connection is either through the meaning indicated by one's own word (<s>svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena</s>), or through the meaning referred to by a pronoun (<s>sarvanāmaparāmṛṣṭārthamukhena</s>).

***NOTES:
#86 Ms: <s>ŚniṣṭārthaŚ</s>;

children.text:
SD
svaśabdanirdiṣṭārthamukhena samanvaye bahavaḥ prakārāḥ, tathā hi yattador
upakramopasaṃhārakramarūpo nityam abhisambandhaḥ. sa ca śābdaḥ, ārthaś ca.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
In the case of connection through the meaning indicated by one's own word, there are many modes. For instance, the connection of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> (relative and correlative), which has the form of a fixed sequence of introduction and conclusion, is invariable. And it is of two kinds: verbal (<s>śābda</s>) and semantic (<s>ārtha</s>).

children.text:
SD
dvayor #87 yattador upādāne sati, śābdaḥ.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
When both <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s> are employed [in the sentence], it is verbal.
SP (verse)
The connection of <s>yat</s> and <s>tat</s>, which has the form of a sequence of introduction and conclusion, /

children.text: yaḥ sambandhaḥ, sa śābdo hi. dvayoḥ śabdena kīrtanam //
children.translated_text: that connection is indeed verbal—[it is] the mention of both through [their respective] words. //

***NOTES:
#87 Ms: <s>dvayo</s>;

SD (prose commentary)
When only one of the two is employed, it is semantic.
SP (verse)
Where there is the employment of only one of <s>yat</s> or <s>tat</s>, /
the implied reference (<s>ākṣepa</s>) of the other, due to the invariable connection, is called semantic. //

children.text:
SD
yadi tasyārthasāmarthyenākṣepāt tacchabdasya #88 kevalopādāne saty, ārthaḥ
(18v:) triprakāraḥ, prasiddhaprakrāntānubhūtavastuviṣayeṇa ca, yacchabdena tasya
sambandhāt.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
If, by the force of the meaning, through implied reference, only one of the <s>tat</s>-word pair is employed, the semantic [connection] is of three kinds: with reference to a well-known object, to a previously mentioned object, and to an experienced object, through the connection of <s>yat</s>-word with it.
SP (verse)

children.text: ākṣepo [']rthād yado yatra nopādānaṃ #89, tadas tadā /
children.translated_text: Where the implied reference is from meaning, and <s>yat</s> is not employed, then <s>tat</s> [is used] at that point; /
the semantic [connection] is threefold: with reference to the well-known, the experienced, and the previously mentioned. //

***NOTES:
#88 Ms: <s>tat tacchadśabdasya</s>; #89 Ś: <s>tūpādānaṃ</s>;

children.text:
SD
yacchabdasya kevalasyopādāne sati, ārtho dvividhas samanvayaḥ, prakrāntavastu-
viṣayeṇa kalpitakarmādiviṣayeṇa ca, tacchabdena tasya sambandhāt.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
When only the <s>yat</s>-word is employed, the semantic connection (<s>samanvaya</s>) is twofold: with reference to a previously mentioned object and with reference to an imagined object such as <s>karman</s> and the like, through the connection of <s>tat</s>-word with it.
SP (verse)
When only <s>yat</s> is employed, with reference to the previously mentioned, that /
semantic [connection] is twofold: also with reference to the imagined object such as action and the like. //
And the reference to an agent stated within the same sentence (<s>ekavākya</s>) by [demonstratives such as] <s>idam</s> and the like, /

children.text: tacchabdena parāmarśo na kāryaḥ kavibhiḥ kvacit //
children.translated_text: should never be made by poets through the <s>tat</s>-word. //

children.text: ya ekasya yadaḥ pūrvaṃ prayogo, duṣṭa eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: The use of <s>yat</s> alone before [its correlative] is indeed faulty; /
for when there is the use of <s>idam</s> and the like, synonymous in meaning [with <s>tat</s>], /

children.text: yadaḥ pūrvaṃ prayoge ca, no doṣo, na #93 guṇas tadā //
children.translated_text: and [<s>yat</s> is] used first, there is neither a fault nor a merit. //

***NOTES:
#90 N: <s>Śviṣaye na</s>; #91 SPS: "<s>tat</s>" means <s>tadā</s>; #92 N: <s>kalpitas tatkarmādiviṣaye na ca</s>; #93 N: <s>na</s> in margina.;

children.text:
SD
kvacic ca kevale kriyāpade 'dhyāhriyamāṇakārakasambandhe sati, vākyārthapari-
samāptir dṛśyate / yathā 'āgaccha, āgaccha. cala, cala. brūhi, brūhi. yāhi, yāhi.
apasarpa, apasarpa. vada, vada'.
children.translated_text:
SD (prose commentary)
And sometimes, when the connection of the <s>kāraka</s> (case relation) being supplied is with the verbal form alone, the completion of sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārthaparasamāpti</s>) is observed. As in '<s>āgaccha, āgaccha</s>' (come, come); '<s>cala, cala</s>' (move, move); '<s>brūhi, brūhi</s>' (speak, speak); '<s>yāhi, yāhi</s>' (go, go); '<s>apasarpa, apasarpa</s>' (withdraw, withdraw); '<s>vada, va[da]</s>' (say, say).
SP (verse)
And the syntactic relation of implied <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) may sometimes occur
even in the employment of a single action, as in 'Speak! Go away, sir!'

***NOTES:
#94 N: -kriyā-;
SD (Prose redaction)

children.translated_text: Here, when the sentence-meaning is completed in a single verse, it is a <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse); when the sentence-meaning is completed

children.text: bhyāṃ #95 vākyārthaparisamāptau yugalakam, tribhis tilakam, caturbhis cakka-
children.translated_text: in two verses, it is a <s>yugalaka</s> (couplet); in three, a <s>tilaka</s> (ornament-trio); in four, a <s>cakka-</s>

children.text: lakam, pañcabhiḥ kulakam, anantaraṃ mahākulakam // etair vyastais samastair vā
children.translated_text: <s>laka</s> (quartet); in five, a <s>kulaka</s> (cluster); beyond that, a <s>mahākulaka</s> (great cluster). By these, whether separate or combined,
a <s>prabandha</s> (literary composition) [is formed]. Thus, auspiciousness.
SP (Verse redaction)
Where the repose of the sentence-meaning is seen in a single verse,

children.text: muktakaṃ tatra #97, yugmena yugalam, tilakaṃ tribhiḥ //
children.translated_text: there it is a <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse); with a pair, a <s>yugala</s> (couplet); with three, a <s>tilaka</s> (trio).

children.text: caturbhiś ca cakkalakaṃ, pañcabhiḥ kulakaṃ smṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: With four, a <s>cakkalaka</s> (quartet); with five, it is known as a <s>kulaka</s> (cluster);
the masters speak of a <s>mahākulaka</s> (great cluster) beyond that.

SD (Prose redaction)
This mere indication of syntactic construction (<s>anvaya</s>) has been illuminated for beginners.
By this direction, beginners become confident in proper syntactic construction.

children.text: pañcake daśake vāpi ślokānāṃ yadi darśyate /
children.translated_text: If it is demonstrated in groups of five or even ten verses,

children.text: bālaś caitat, tatas samyaganvayam #98 prati muktadhīḥ //
children.translated_text: even a beginner, from that, [becomes] one whose mind is liberated with regard to proper syntactic construction.
Thus the <s>Samanvayadik</s> (Direction on Syntactic Construction) is concluded. This is the work of the scholar <s>Chuḍḍaka</s> (Kuḍaka), the king's paṇḍita.
SP (Verse redaction)
This <s>Samanvayapradīpa</s> (Lamp of Syntactic Construction), following the path stated by <s>Kuḍaka</s>, by me
has been shown. The learned should here supply what has been missed.
(Commentary:) '<s>Kuḍaka</s>' is a certain scholar. 'The path stated by him' means the specific treatise

children.text: samanvayadigākhyo #100 granthaviśeṣa ity arthaḥ. sa tu gadyarūpeṇa sthito,
children.translated_text: called <s>Samanvayadik</s> — this is the meaning. That [treatise] stands in prose form,
while this [version]

children.text: yaṃ tu padyarūpeṇaitāvān eva viśeṣaḥ // samāpto [']yaṃ
children.translated_text: is in verse form — just this is the only difference. This

children.text:
samanvayapradīpasaṅketaḥ vibudhasamūhavanditapādapadmasya
śrīgaṅgādharasvāminaḥ śiṣyeṇa paṇḍitadevaśarmaṇā iti bhadram #101.
children.translated_text: <s>Samanvayapradīpa</s> compendium is concluded, [composed] by the scholar <s>Devaśarman</s>, disciple of the illustrious <s>Gaṅgādharasvāmin</s>, whose lotus-feet are venerated by assemblies of the learned. Blessings.
